desc: The most consequential document in this domain and the first time Congress has formally interrogated an FFRDC operator about UAP holdings. Dated 22 May 2026, ten pages, obtained by DefenseScoop and announced by Burlison's office on 26 May. It directs MITRE to identify and preserve all records connected to unidentified anomalous phenomena, including 'unexplained aerospace or undersea events, technologies of unknown origin, and alleged crash-retrieval or reverse-engineering programs', together with Special and Controlled Access Programs, sensor data, materials analysis and classification guides - reaching back to 1930. It contains more than forty production requests, including work involving Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Raytheon, Boeing, General Dynamics, SAIC and Leidos, and covers UAP detection and tracking across air, space, maritime, cyber and electromagnetic domains. It sets a schedule: designate a senior responsible officer within 5 business days; issue a preservation hold within 10 business days; coordinate a classified briefing for cleared committee staff within 14 days; deliver written responses and a records-location index within 30 days; produce unclassified materials in native electronic format with complete metadata within 45 days. MITRE must also account for records created, handled, transferred, withheld or destroyed by the corporation, its FFRDCs or its subcontractors. The rationale is stated in FFRDC terms: 'FFRDCs often receive special access to government facilities, data, sponsor requirements, and sensitive technical information that ordinary private contractors may not receive', and 'They cannot become private vaults for federal records - especially records Congress has directed to be identified, preserved, reviewed, and transferred for public release.' Burlison also states the standard of proof he is applying: 'This inquiry does not require MITRE to accept any particular conclusion about the origin or nature of UAP. It requires MITRE to tell Congress what it knows, what it holds, what it has held, what it has transferred, what it has destroyed or was directed to destroy, and which federal sponsors or classification authorities control any responsive records.' MITRE's answer, that it would coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work, is the FFRDC structure asserting itself.

dossier.denialPosture: MITRE has not denied holding responsive records. Its only public statement — that if relevant material is found it will 'coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work to determine how to best provide any assets' — asserts a custodial rather than a disclosing posture, positioning the sponsor agency, not Congress, as the recipient. That is precisely the routing Burlison's letter anticipated and attempted to foreclose by demanding that MITRE identify the sponsor, the classification authority and 'the shortest practical path to lawful disclosure to Congress and transfer to NARA.'
dossier.narrative:
Burlison's MITRE package is the moment the congressional inquiry stopped asking the Pentagon and started asking the people who hold the Pentagon's files.

The premise is stated in the cover letter's second paragraph. MITRE operates multiple FFRDCs, and 'By design, FFRDCs often receive special access to government facilities, data, sponsor requirements, and sensitive technical information that ordinary private contractors may not receive. This special public-trust role makes records stewardship, sponsor accountability, and congressional visibility especially important.' The statutory hook is sections 1841-1843 of the FY2024 NDAA and NARA's Record Group 615: if government-funded UAP records sit in a contractor's archive, the statute reaches them, and MITRE's status as a nonprofit operator does not create a safe harbor. DefenseScoop reported that FFRDCs are largely shielded from public disclosure by FOIA exemptions, and that some officials have warned this lets them hold government information the public has a right to see.

The scope is deliberately enormous. 'Unless otherwise specified, the relevant time period is January 1, 1930, to the present.' MITRE was incorporated in 1958; the 1930 start date is a trap for inherited archives, telling MITRE that if it contends the request is overbroad for a legacy period it must 'identify the earliest date for which MITRE can search reliably, the reason older records cannot be searched, and the custodian or sponsor most likely to hold the older records.' The definition of 'UAP-related' extends to any record 'described, coded, compartmented, or euphemized as involving' UAP, UFO, USO, transmedium craft, advanced aerospace threat, technology of unknown origin, non-human intelligence, legacy crash retrieval, crash retrieval, reverse engineering, recovered vehicle, recovered material, biological material, 'or equivalent terms.' Euphemism is named as a category of evidence.

The deadlines are tight and sequenced. Within five business days, designate a vice-president-level officer to coordinate. Within ten business days, issue and confirm a written preservation hold covering 'restricted systems, air-gapped environments, classified repositories, personal workspaces used for official business, archived systems, email, collaboration platforms, backup media, contractor/subcontractor systems, and offsite storage.' Within fourteen days, contact the office to coordinate a classified briefing for Task Force Members and cleared Committee staff at 'the appropriate TS/SCI/SAP level.' Within thirty days, written answers plus a records-location index naming repositories, custodians, contract vehicles, sponsors, classification authorities and record schedules. Within forty-five days, production of all unclassified responsive records in native electronic format with complete metadata, plus a segregated classified annex and a privilege and classification log. The letter warns that 'False statements, concealment, alteration, destruction, or obstruction in connection with this inquiry may implicate federal law, including but not limited to 18 U.S.C. §§ 1001, 1505, 1512, 1519, and 2071.'

The eleven enclosure sections read as a taxonomy of how a program stays hidden. Section I demands an accounting of records destroyed, degaussed, sanitized, reclassified, moved to a restricted system or 'placed under sponsor control,' with the authority and the responsible personnel named. Section II demands identification of every contract, IDIQ, GWAC, BPA, OTA and CRADA under which MITRE touched UAP information, and every individual involved with 'their specific functions and duties' — and names AARO, the UAP Task Force, AATIP, AAWSAP, DIA, CIA, NSA, NRO, NGA, ONI, NRL, DARPA, IARPA and DOE laboratories, 'or any successor, predecessor, cover, compartment, or renamed activity.' Section II.6 asks whether MITRE 'provided cover' for another entity's UAP work.

Section III is the compartmentation audit already described. Section IV asks what MITRE has and has not sent to NARA under the UAP Records Collection. Section V asks for sensor work across radar, optical, infrared, acoustic and undersea domains, expressly including 'SOSUS/IUSS-related' systems and 'unidentified submerged objects.' Section VI asks about recovered anomalous materials, isotope ratios, chain of custody, metamaterials, propulsion and 'cognitive interface systems' — and, in VI.4, about 'biological material, biological samples, human physiological effects, medical monitoring, occupational exposure, anomalous injury, cognitive or neurological effects, or environmental hazards associated with UAP-related materials, objects, fields, occupants, or events,' with the careful caveat that the request 'seeks records and safety documentation only and does not presume the validity of any particular biological claim.' The word 'occupants' is doing a great deal of work in a congressional document.

Section VII asks for SCIFs, SAPFs, vaults and 'material-containment work.' Section VIII asks for internal disclosures, retaliation, and nondisclosure instruments 'beyond standard government-secrecy obligations' that restricted personnel from reporting to Congress, IGs, AARO, NARA or law enforcement. Section IX names Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Raytheon/RRTX, Boeing, General Dynamics, SAIC, Leidos, Battelle, The Aerospace Corporation, Booz Allen Hamilton, BAE Systems and Bigelow Aerospace or its successors. Section X goes at the money. Section XI demands a certified response signed by a responsible MITRE officer and counsel.

MITRE's answer, given to DefenseScoop on 27 May 2026, was custodial rather than responsive: 'If any relevant material is found, we will coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work to determine how to best provide any assets.' That is a statement that anything found goes back to the sponsor, not to Congress. A member of Burlison's staff told DefenseScoop the letter was informed by 'advice from many whistleblowers, disclosure advocacy organizations, and those working at FFRDCs.'

The MITRE package was not the first shot. On 7 May 2026 Burlison had written to MIT Lincoln Laboratory Director Melissa G. Choi and counsel David A. Suski about a single object: a reel-to-reel recording catalogued as 'AF-ATIC-FILM, 03/52' from the Beacon Hill Study, labeled 'flying saucer talk,' with Edward J. Ruppelt — then head of Project Blue Book — listed as the briefer. That letter demanded the laboratory determine whether the recording is extant, preserve it, digitize it to preservation grade, and transmit it with metadata to NARA for Record Group 615. It also instructed the laboratory to coordinate with the cognizant sponsor, the original classification authority, ISOO and the Public Interest Declassification Board if an active Security Classification Guide still applies to a 1952 tape.

dossier.whatItIs: A ten-page package of legislative interrogatories and production requests dated 22 May 2026, sent by Rep. Eric Burlison (R-MO-07) to Dr. Mark Peters, President and Chief Executive Officer, and Christopher Land, Senior Vice President and General Counsel, of The MITRE Corporation at 7525 Colshire Drive, McLean, Virginia. Copied to Task Force Chairwoman Anna Paulina Luna, Oversight Chairman James Comer, and Michael D. Thomas, Director of the Information Security Oversight Office at NARA. The enclosure runs eleven numbered sections and more than forty specific requests, with a relevant time period beginning 1 January 1930.
dossier.whyImplicated: This is the first congressional instrument that treats a federally funded research and development center as a potential custodian of the legacy program's paper. It does not ask MITRE whether UAP are real. It asks MITRE which Special Access Programs, Controlled Access Programs, Alternative Compensatory Control Measures, Managed-Need-To-Know codewords, DOE Restricted Data compartments and SIGMA categories it participated in touching UAP subject matter, and for each one, 'whether the program was reported to the appropriate congressional committees.' It asks for any classification guide, nondisclosure agreement or sponsor communication that instructed MITRE personnel to avoid the words UAP, UFO, USO, crash retrieval, reverse engineering, technology of unknown origin or non-human intelligence in their records. It asks for funding routed through 'a cover program' whose 'public description differed materially from the responsive work performed,' and for funding MITRE understood to be 'hidden from, not briefed to, or not readily visible to ordinary sponsor budget channels.' And it names twelve companies by name. The letter is a map of the concealment hypothesis rendered as a document request.

entityInfo.desc: The compliance schedule, in full, as reported by MeriTalk and DefenseScoop from the letter text: designate a senior officer responsible for the response within 5 business days; issue a litigation-style preservation hold within 10 business days; coordinate a classified briefing for cleared committee staff within 14 days; deliver written responses and a records-location index within 30 days; produce unclassified materials in native electronic format with complete metadata within 45 days; and separately identify all classified or sponsor-controlled materials with the controlling authority named. MITRE must account for records created, handled, transferred, withheld or destroyed by the corporation, by any of its six FFRDCs, or by its subcontractors. Coverage extends to UAP detection and tracking across air, space, maritime, cyber and electromagnetic domains, and to MITRE work involving Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Raytheon, Boeing, General Dynamics, SAIC and Leidos. The temporal reach - back to 1930 - is unusual and deliberate: it predates MITRE's own 1958 founding, which means the request captures predecessor and inherited holdings including anything that travelled with the 485 staff who came from MIT Lincoln Laboratory. Counting from 22 May 2026, the 45-day unclassified production deadline fell on approximately 6 July 2026 and the 30-day index deadline on approximately 21 June 2026. As of 12 August 2026 no public production, index, or classified briefing outcome has been reported, and Burlison's office has not announced non-compliance. That silence is the open item on this board.

timeline.label: The MITRE demand
timeline.text: Burlison sends MITRE a ten-page letter with 40+ production requests covering UAP, anomalous materials and reverse engineering back to 1930, due in 45 days in native format with metadata.

timeline.label: Burlison's 10-page production request to MITRE
timeline.text: The first congressional records demand ever addressed to an FFRDC operator on UAP: more than 40 requests covering crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering programmes, Special and Controlled Access Programs, sensor data and materials analysis back to 1930.

timeline.label: Burlison demands MITRE's UAP records back to 1930
timeline.text: A ten-page letter with over 40 production requests, a 45-day deadline, native electronic format with complete metadata, naming eleven other contractors in scope. MITRE says it will coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work.

timeline.label: MITRE's 45-day production deadline falls
timeline.text: No public production has been reported as of 12 August 2026 in response to Burlison's 22 May demand for records back to 1930.
